policies.title: Rwandan ordinary passports: named visa-free short visits
policies.summary: Rwanda DGIE's live ordinary-passport column records Visa not required for the Democratic Republic of the Congo and São Tomé and Príncipe.
conditions: This is limited to the two retained named rows in DGIE's ordinary-passport column; it is not inferred from regional membership, a portal, or an omitted nationality.

The live list has no publication or revision date. It supports the matching fallback rows but should be rechecked if Rwanda DGIE publishes a dated replacement or a destination authority publishes a contrary current rule.
Stay period, purpose limits, special passports, carrier requirements and final admission remain separate.

unresolved.reason: Rwanda DGIE's undated table says visa not required, while Jordan's current Tourism Ministry guidance describes a paid arrival visa for all nationalities subject to advance-visa exceptions. The public sources conflict and do not map Rwanda into the exception mechanism, so neither status is promoted.
No current Afghan or Rwandan government source establishes an ordinary Rwandan-passport short-visitor route and its issuance timing. Operational restrictions are not a taxonomy status.

DGIE's undated live list says visa upon arrival, but Cabo Verde's current government schedules and corrected 2026 Gazette annex do not establish an ordinary Rwandan-passport arrival route. EASE registration and generic border competence are not nationality eligibility or issuance proof.
Current Comorian law describes visas but no current competent authority publishes an ordinary Rwandan-passport exemption, electronic, advance, or arrival-issued visitor rule.

DGIE's undated live list says Visa not required, but Grenada's only nationality schedule remains expressly updated February 2021. No later Grenadian Immigration, Gazette, legislation or current-force source corroborates the ordinary-passport baseline.
Iran's current MFA portal has generic application and named exception material but no current ordinary Rwandan-passport route. A portal and omissions do not establish eligibility or issuance timing.
Iraq's current federal sources and eVisa portal do not produce a positive ordinary Rwandan-passport visitor decision. Kurdistan Region material is not used for a federal baseline.

Kuwait Interior data exposes visitor products but no positive controlling ordinary Rwandan tourist-nationality decision. GCC-resident, profession, sponsor and third-country-document routes are excluded.
Kyrgyzstan's eVisa selector requires a positive country and document result, which was not recoverable for this ordinary passport. Generic eVisa availability is not eligibility evidence.
No retrievable current Libyan or Rwandan government source establishes an ordinary Rwandan-passport visitor route and actual issuance timing.
Myanmar's current tourist eVisa and waiver cohorts do not name this ordinary passport. Omission, generic online application, and consular fallback are not a nationality-specific complement.
No current DPRK or Rwandan primary source establishes an ordinary Rwandan-passport visitor route. Operational access restrictions cannot be normalized to a visa status.
North Macedonia's live country checker did not yield a reproducible Rwandan ordinary-passport decision, and no current operative nationality regulation was recovered.
Fresh Omani ROP eligibility sessions do not establish an unconditional individual tourist product for this nationality; family, property and special-purpose paths are excluded.
Israeli crossing and permit controls do not establish a Palestine-only ordinary Rwandan-passport visitor baseline, and no Palestinian authority publishes one.
No current Panamanian or Rwandan official nationality schedule establishes an ordinary Rwandan-passport visitor baseline. Conditional third-country-document routes are excluded.

Saudi Arabia's live eligibility data marks the nationality ineligible for the unconditional tourist route; available U.S./UK/Schengen or GCC-residence paths are conditional. No advance-visa complement is inferred.

DGIE says visa upon arrival, but Sierra Leone's live official material conflicts between emailed eVisa issuance and airport-issued descriptions. No source resolves actual issuance timing for this ordinary passport.
Current Solomon Islands Immigration material conflicts between electronic processing and manual in-person applications, while arrival issuance is discretionary and not nationality-mapped.
Sudan Passport Directorate material describes visitor categories and counter processing but supplies no ordinary Rwandan-passport eligibility or prior-approval schedule.
Syria's current aviation material requires an advance visa unless exempt but gives no ordinary-passport nationality schedule; its online service does not establish electronic issuance.
Trinidad and Tobago's current waiver material does not give a positive Rwandan ordinary-passport result, and no visa-required complement is inferred from omission or portal availability.
Tunisia's current consular material establishes a visa process and treaty-qualified waivers but no current ordinary Rwandan-passport schedule or effective agreement register.

Turkmenistan's general entry-visa rule preserves treaty exceptions but no current ordinary Rwandan-passport exemption or unconditional issuance route is published. Invitation or preapproval paths are excluded.

DGIE says Visa not required, but Vanuatu DIPS's live nationality material places Rwanda in inconsistent cohorts. Its tourist rules distinguish arrival issuance for exempt countries from advance approval for non-exempt countries, so the conflict cannot be normalized.
